title: Intelligence Brief - May 24, 2026
summary: Five investigative threads moved in the 24-hour window. (1) Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty's conflict-of-interest disclosure is now seven months past the statutory filing deadline -- every other Carney cabinet member has filed -- making this a direct Conflict of Interest Act s.20-22 breach at cabinet level. (2) The special joint MAID committee is being publicly described as biased by Canada's leading assisted-dying expert: co-chairs (Liberal MP Marcus Powlowski + Conservative Senator Yonah Martin) are both opposed to the 2027 mental-illness extension, the expert says the committee is 'hearing testimony unrelated to its mandate', and heads of psychiatry at 13 Canadian medical schools wrote requesting the federal government halt the expansion entirely. PM Carney is withholding position. (3) Defence Minister David McGuinty introduced a National Defence Act amendment that would remove military jurisdiction over sexual offence investigations and prosecutions; an Ontario MOU for civilian-justice transfers has been signed. (4) Senators (one-third of the Senate) joined in calling for a thorough investigation of Canadian arms reaching Israel; Israel Tax Authority customs records detail 2025 imports of Canadian 'bullets' and three Montreal-Dorval -> Tel Aviv-Yafo cartridge shipments (Sept 2024, May 2025, July 2025). Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand's office calls the report 'flawed and misleading.' (5) Bill C-9 (Combatting Hate Act) Senate review pending after House 188-144 passage; religious exemption removed via Bloc amendment; CCLA: risks criminalizing peaceful protest.

stories.title: Gull-Masty conflict-of-interest disclosure 7 months overdue -- cabinet-level CoIA breach
stories.summary: Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty is the only Carney cabinet member whose public conflict-of-interest disclosure remains absent from the ethics commissioner's public registry seven months after the statutory filing deadline. Direct breach of Conflict of Interest Act s.20-22 reporting timelines. Adds to existing dossier on Carney's own 100+-entity Brookfield-tied screen and the late-April ETHI committee report recommending forced PM divestiture within 60 days of assuming office.
stories.connection: Updates carney_conflicts_dossier.json + ethics_matrix_dossier.json. Adds Gull-Masty to cabinet-tier accountability tracking.

stories.title: MAID committee bias allegation + 13 medical schools urge halt
stories.summary: Special joint committee co-chairs Liberal MP Marcus Powlowski and Conservative Senator Yonah Martin are both publicly opposed to the 2027 mental-illness MAID extension. Canada's leading assisted-dying expert: the committee is 'hearing testimony unrelated to its mandate' and is 'heavily weighted toward people opposed.' Heads of psychiatry at 13 Canadian medical schools wrote requesting the federal government halt the expansion. PM Carney withholding position: 'I like to take informed positions and I'll wait for the report.'
stories.connection: Updates maid_investigation_report.json. The bias allegation is itself evidence the parliamentary deliberation process is compromised.

stories.title: McGuinty introduces NDA amendment to strip military of sexual offence jurisdiction; Ontario MOU signed
stories.summary: Defence Minister David McGuinty introduced legislation amending the National Defence Act to remove the Canadian military's jurisdiction to investigate and prosecute sexual offences. Memorandum of Understanding signed with Ontario for civilian-justice transfers; McGuinty says progress 'quite encouraging.' Pairs with January 2026 Ontario Superior Court stay (military police evidence-tampering, judge cited 'wilful police misconduct') and the watchdog finding that military police 'rushed to judgment' before an air-force officer's suicide (supervisor was drunk at the time, victim interview unrecorded). Two military police officers suspended pending the misconduct investigation following the ONSC ruling.
stories.connection: Federal-government acknowledgement that military jurisdiction over sexual offences is structurally broken.

stories.title: 32 senators call for arms-to-Israel investigation; Israel Tax Authority records 3 Dorval-Tel Aviv shipments
stories.summary: Senator Yuen Pau Woo led 32 senators -- one-third of the chamber -- in a formal call for a thorough investigation of what Canadian military hardware is actually reaching Israel. Israel Tax Authority customs records detail 2025 imports of Canadian 'bullets' and military hardware that Ottawa says it has not authorized for export. Three documented shipments of 'cartriges' flew from Montreal-Dorval to Tel Aviv-Yafo in September 2024, May 2025, and July 2025. Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand's office calls the report 'flawed' and says its findings are 'misleading and significantly misrepresent the facts.'
stories.connection: Direct update to arms_exports_israel.json and dossier_senator_woo.json. Material to Rome Statute Article 25(3)(c) aiding-and-abetting analysis. The 32-senator coalition is the largest formal political pressure to date on the arms-to-Israel transparency question.

stories.title: Bill C-9 (Combatting Hate Act) Senate review pending after House 188-144 passage
stories.summary: Bill C-9 passed House of Commons 188-144 with Bloc support secured by removing the religious exemption from the Criminal Code hate-speech provisions. CPC and NDP voted against. Up to 10-year sentences for obstructing access to places of worship or other identifiable-group gathering sites. CCLA: 'risks criminalizing peaceful protest.' Senate may still amend. No movement on Senate passage as of this filing. CIJA disclosed 73 contacts during JUST committee review.
stories.connection: Updates ai-research.html + 5gw-subversion.html. Pairs with cija_lobbying_detail.json. Senate amendment opportunity is the last legislative pressure point before law.
